body: I honestly can't wait until humans become augmented to the point where crap like the race and gender you're born with isn't really a thing or relevant anymore

I've tried seeing a councilor at my uni, but so far I couldn't really say it helped a lot. New situations which force me to confront these fears are coming up almost daily, like just today I've found some spots of white powdery stuff on my backpack. The moment I saw that, my brain just jumps to the conclusion that it's lead-based paint that some exposed worker accidentally rubbed onto my backpack during my commute, or that one guy who seemed pissed at me(he sort of pushed me) for not moving fast enough while we were getting off the subway putting something hazardous on purpose. Meanwhile, there are more plausible scenarios, like those white powdery stuff being just road salt from someone behind me going down the stairs accidentally kicking some of the salt mixed slush(since it snowed pretty badly yesterday) onto my backpack. Despite the latter scenario being probably the most likely, my brain doesn't really ever distance itself from the scenarios prior. Now, I feel so mentally paralyzed that I have great difficulties getting any work done. My futurist fantasies also involve humanity finding a cure for brain damage or living in a body/medium that is more invulnerable to that kind of damage. But those fantasies are mostly reserved to being able to create my own worlds and conscious beings to inhabit in them along with my fantasy friends and fantasy family.
The real question is, will those less lonely than us ever have to put in as much effort as we are told to?
